title: How to write a service agreement for a house cleaning job
summary: Paste your cleaning job details into ChatGPT and get a simple service agreement. Check every room, the price, and the cancel rule before you send it.

tests.prompt:
You help a cleaning business owner write a simple service agreement for one house. Draft only. This is not legal advice. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Property address: [ADDRESS]
Type of cleaning: [SERVICE TYPE]
Rooms or areas: [AREAS]
What's included: [INCLUDED]
What's not included: [NOT INCLUDED]
Visit frequency: [FREQUENCY]
Price: [PRICE]
How they pay and when: [PAYMENT]
Cancellation or reschedule rule: [CANCEL RULE]
Supplies and access: [SUPPLIES AND ACCESS]
Start date: [START DATE]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- This is a simple service agreement, not a legal form. Do not invent legal clauses, liability waivers, or insurance language.
- Do not add rooms, add-on services, or fees that are not in the details.
- Do not change the price or the cancellation rule. Copy them exactly.
- Use plain words a homeowner can read once. Short sentences. No legalese.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Title
Parties and address
The service
What's included
What's not included
Schedule and price
Payment
Cancellation
Supplies and access
Start date
How to agree (a short line asking them to reply "agreed" or sign)
Facts used
Unknown
Keep the agreement under 280 words.

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: Write the customer name, address, type of clean, rooms, what's included and not, how often you visit, the price, how they pay, and your cancellation rule.
Add how you get in, who brings supplies, the start date, and your name and phone.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN if a rule is not decided yet.
Read the agreement beside your notes. Confirm rooms, price, payment, and the cancel rule. Delete any legal clause, fee, or room you did not write.
Send it as an email or a document for the customer to reply 'agreed' or sign, and only start the job after they agree.
setup.approvalStep: You check the rooms, the price, and the cancellation rule, then you send the agreement yourself. This is a plain summary of what you already offer, not legal advice.
failureModes: The draft adds legal language, liability waivers, or insurance claims you did not provide. Take those sentences out.
A room or add-on appears that you did not include in the price. Remove it or price it separately.
The cancellation rule or the price does not match what you told the customer. Put your real terms back in.
The access notes invent a lockbox code. Never add a code that was not in your notes.

faq.a: No. It is a plain summary of the work, the price, and your cancel rule, written so both of you can agree. If you need a formal contract, have a lawyer review one. Do not let the draft invent legal clauses.

faq.q: What if I do not have a cancellation rule yet?
faq.a: Leave that line blank so it is marked UNKNOWN, then decide and add it before you send the agreement. A clear 24-hour or 48-hour rule prevents most surprises.

faq.q: Can I use this for a one-time deep clean?
faq.a: Yes. Set the service type and frequency to a one-time visit, and list the extra deep-clean tasks in What's included.

job: Paste cleaning job details and get a simple service agreement a homeowner can agree to.
who: Cleaning business owners who want a plain one-page agreement that lists the work, the price, and how to cancel.

example.scenario: A cleaner is starting a biweekly clean at a two-bedroom apartment and wants the terms in writing before the first visit.
example.input:
Customer name: Jamie Cole
Property address: 5 South Alley, Apt 2B
Type of cleaning: Recurring standard clean
Rooms or areas: Kitchen, living room, two bedrooms, one bathroom, and hallway
What's included: Floors, counters, bathroom fixtures, kitchen sink, and emptying trash
What's not included: Inside the oven, inside the fridge, windows, and laundry
Visit frequency: Every other Tuesday, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Price: $140 per visit
How they pay and when: Card on file, charged the day of the visit
Cancellation or reschedule rule: 24 hours notice or the visit is charged
Supplies and access: I bring supplies. Key is in the lockbox. Code already shared by text.
Start date: November 18
Your name and business: Robin at Open Window Cleaning
Your phone: 555-0133
example.output:
Title: House cleaning service agreement

Parties and address: Open Window Cleaning (Robin) and Jamie Cole, for 5 South Alley, Apt 2B.

The service: A recurring standard clean every other Tuesday, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., starting November 18.

What's included: Floors, counters, bathroom fixtures, kitchen sink, and emptying trash in the kitchen, living room, two bedrooms, one bathroom, and hallway.

What's not included: Inside the oven, inside the fridge, windows, and laundry.

Schedule and price: $140 per visit.

Payment: Card on file, charged the day of the visit.

Cancellation: If you need to cancel or move a visit, give 24 hours notice. After that, the visit is charged.

Supplies and access: Open Window Cleaning brings supplies and will use the lockbox key already shared by text.

Start date: November 18.

How to agree: Reply to this email with the word agreed, or sign and send it back, and I will put November 18 on the calendar.

Facts used: Apt 2B, $140, every other Tuesday, 24 hours, November 18.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up job terms, only to show a plain agreement. This is not legal advice.
